item.title: Property downturn spreads to 93pc of suburbs in Australia's capital cities
item.description: Australian house prices have fallen for a fifth straight month, according to property data firm Cotality. It says the downturn has now spread to 93 per cent of suburbs in the nation's capital cities.

item.title: Football great Lionel Messi announces retirement from Argentina team
item.description: The announcement comes just weeks after the death of his father Jorge, after which he expressed doubts about the future of his international career.

item.title: Donald Trump slams US data centre backlash, saying China 'could not be happier'
item.description: The US president warns American voters they "will only have yourselves to blame" if they kill off data centre development, as the issue gains traction ahead of the midterms.

item.title: Travel quiz September 1: Take a trip with us
item.description: What's the longest flight time between Australian capitals? And which US state is home to the birthplace of rock'n'roll, Memphis?

item.title: What is 'career minimalism' and what are the potential rewards and risks?
item.description: "Career minimalism" may have found its way to your algorithm, but this is what experts say about the rewards and risks.

item.title: Should you consent to your child's school publishing their images?
item.description: If you don't like the idea of your child's face appearing in the school newsletter or Facebook page, you can refuse consent. But experts warn there can be social consequences for children.

item.title: China warns of 'consequences' over Taiwan's presence at Pacific Islands Forum leaders meeting
item.description: There are concerns tensions between China and Taiwan could explode into the open at this year's meeting, distracting from the key Pacific priorities.

item.title: Facial recognition technology 'scope creep' is upon us, experts warn
item.description: Industry groups say the move to facial scans in supermarkets is about safety, but analysts say that once the technology is installed, its "scope creep" paves the way for options like discriminatory pricing.

item.title: Scandal-plagued KPMG starts to pay the bill for its mistakes
item.description: In the wake of scandals about the misuse of confidential information, embattled consulting firm KPMG is losing million-dollar contracts and cutting its workforce. And that's all before the corporate regulator, ASIC, has even opened its mouth.

item.title: Granville rail disaster first responders among NSW recipients of 2026 Australian Bravery Decorations
item.description: First responders at the Granville rail disaster are being recognised with Australian Bravery Decorations, almost 50 years after the nation's worst train crash.

item.title: South Australian government defies Albanese, urges change to voluntary assisted dying telehealth laws
item.description: South Australia has become the first state to formally urge the Commonwealth to change a federal law preventing doctors from using telehealth in voluntary assisted dying (VAD).

item.title: Nepali survivors 'have nothing' on return to unrecognisable villages
item.description: The ABC sees villages buried under mud, locals sheltering in school halls with no running water, and aid workers racing against time to stop disease spreading.

item.title: Clifftop at Hepburn properties allegedly installed without permission, prompting council dispute
item.description: Luxury tourist villas being offered for hundreds of dollars a night were allegedly installed in a bushfire-prone area without prior permission, an ABC investigation has found.

item.title: Netanyahu's rhetoric on latest settler violence doesn't match action from Israeli government
item.description: If the Israeli prime minister sees settler violence as a "grave injustice", why can't one of the most powerful militaries in the world stop it from happening? The answer, as it often does, comes down to politics.

item.title: Time running out for teen brain cancer patient hoping to access world-first mRNA vaccine trial
item.description: A world-first mRNA vaccine trial offers some hope to the family of a teenager dying from brain cancer, but they worry he will miss out on a place.

item.title: Queensland records its highest ever annual number of drug overdose deaths
item.description: Advocates say drug overdoses are "costing us people we shouldn't be losing" as unintentional drug-induced deaths surpass 2,000 for the first time.

item.title: Concerns women will fall through the cracks when Hobart's mother-baby unit replaced
item.description: While the mother-baby unit in Hobart deals with complex mental health challenges, staff have been told mothers must be "psychologically well" to be eligible for the service set to replace it.

item.title: Sixty years ago, 'metal boxes' threatened to take over jobs. Now AI is
item.description: In 1968, Australians were warned that computers could wipe out entire professions. Now, a similar conversation is unfolding about artificial intelligence.

item.title: MotoGP circuit in Adelaide reveals Labor's parklands angst, divides green opponents
item.description: The Malinauskas government's grand unveiling of its MotoGP track showed just how much pressure it faced over the environment. It's also opened up a fracture in the green movement.

item.title: Kim Birrell, Alexei Popyrin and Maya Joint advance to second round at US Open in New York
item.description: Gritty Kim Birrell has overcome a match point and a restless night's sleep to break her first-round jinx with a maiden US Open victory in New York.

item.title: Aryna Sabalenka, Carlos Alcaraz begin US Open title defence, Lois Boisson smashes racquet
item.description: Frenchwoman Lois Boisson has provided the first big blow-up of the US Open, smashing her racquet in disgust after going down in three sets to American 26th seed Emma Navarro.

item.title: Fracked gas from Beetaloo Basin will flow to Northern Territory power grid as of today
item.description: As of today, gas fracked from the Beetaloo Basin will flow into the Northern Territory's power grid, with the CLP forecasting the project will generate billions in economic value. But environmental activists say many Territorians oppose the project.

item.title: Man shot dead during home invasion at Glen Alpine, south-west of Sydney
item.description: A man believed to be in his 20s has been shot dead during a "targeted" home invasion south-west of Sydney, police say.

item.title: Hundreds feared stuck in hydropower tunnels as flood deaths pass 950 in Nepal and China
item.description: Rescuers are racing to free hundreds of workers believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites since last week's catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-China border, as the death toll passes 950 with more than 4,400 people missing.

item.title: Hobart City Council votes against abandoning Battery Point walkway proposal
item.description: A proposal for a waterfront walkway around Hobart's historic Battery Point suburb has been debated for decades. The plan has lived to see another day, despite the local council's CEO recommending it be abandoned.

item.title: Live: Oil prices surge on latest US-Iran flare-up, ASX slips as housing slump continues
item.description: The latest flare-up in hostilities between the US and Iran have led to a 3 per cent surge in the oil price. The Australian share market slips while house prices are falling in most of the nation's capital cities. Follow the day's events on the ABC News live markets blog.

item.title: Supreme Court lets White House continue construction on Trump's $558 million ballroom
item.description: A divided Supreme Court has allowed the White House to continue construction on a $558 million ballroom project as lawsuits play out, a win for US President Donald Trump as he remakes the capital in his image.

item.title: Dollyfest announced after Dolly Parton laid to rest at private service
item.description: The estate behind the icon, who died of cancer last week at age 80, announces Dollyfest, a two-day festival across two consecutive weekends in 2027.

item.title: Unification Church leader Hak Ja Han sentenced to two years for corruption
item.description: A South Korean court sentences an 83-year-old church leader to two years in prison for bribing the wife of ousted conservative president Yoon Suk Yeol as well as other corruption charges.

item.title: Locals say illegal firewood trade harming Western Australia's southern forests
item.description: Residents, businesses and community leaders say the sound of chainsaws and the sight of newly felled trees are becoming too frequent, and they want tougher action.

item.title: Drugs allegedly found hidden in breakfast sandwich
item.description: Follow the latest headlines from ABC News, Australia's most trusted media source, with live events, audio and on-demand video from the national broadcaster.

item.title: Marnus Labuschagne dropped as Australia names ODI squad for African series
item.description: Australia has named its ODI squad for its back-to-back series in Zimbabwe and South Africa later this month, with five players dropped, including World Cup winner Marnus Labuschagne.

item.title: Lionel Messi retired from Argentina once, but returned for a decade of dominance and success
item.description: Lionel Messi ends his international football career as a living legend with a God-like status in his country, but the dizzying heights the great man reached almost never happened if he had stuck to his original retirement.

item.title: Liberals promise new hybrid trains for Melbourne's west
item.description: The Victorian Liberals have made a pre-election promise to deliver 25 new hybrid trains for the Melton and Wyndham Vale lines, to service a rapidly growing population.

item.title: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis convicted in 1996 killing of Tupac Shakur
item.description: A jury has found a former gang leader guilty of murder after a trial heard he was the mastermind behind the 1996 drive-by killing of legendary hip-hop artist Tupac Shakur.

item.title: Canberrans suing ACT government costing tens of millions each year as medical negligence costs rise
item.description: The ACT government paid out more than $60 millions in damages, settlements, and legal costs for medical negligence claims in the 2025-26 financial year, more than double the same costs in 2023-24.

item.title: India's Modi tells Russia's Putin that the war in Ukraine must end for humanity's sake
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has told Russian President Vladimir Putin the war in Ukraine needs to end for humanity's sake

item.title: Stefanos Tsitsipas says Nick Kyrgios's suspension for drug use was 'pretty much expected'
item.description: Stefanos Tsitsipas says he was not surprised when it was revealed that Nick Kyrgios had been suspended after testing positive to cocaine.

item.title: Bird flu spreads in Tasmania as vaccination of orange-bellied parrots begins
item.description: H5 bird flu has now been detected across Tasmania, with vaccination efforts for captive orange-bellied parrots, which are critically endangered, getting underway.

item.title: Meth found hidden in a McMuffin during Broome traffic stop, police allege
item.description: Broome detectives allegedly find more than just a protein filling in a McDonald's breakfast item in one of two drug-related incidents linked to fast food in a month.

item.title: Police officer charged with four counts of assault following arrest of teen in Melbourne's west
item.description: Victoria's anti-corruption watchdog has charged a police officer with four counts of assault linked to an arrest in Melbourne's west last year.

item.title: Living with OCD made me feel like I was broken
item.description: Matthew Wright says to many in his life he appeared calm and capable, while he was privately spending hours each day trapped in compulsions.

item.title: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll steps down after 18 months in job
item.description: One of the highest-ranking civilian US military leaders departs, reportedly following tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

item.title: Cronulla Sharks want to play their home NRL finals match at Shark Park
item.description: Cameron McInnes would not be surprised to see the NRL deny Cronulla a home final at Shark Park, warning players were now used to head office making rule changes "at the drop of a hat".

item.title: Motor neurone disease notification may help solve mystery about NSW hotpots
item.description: It is hoped new data from mandatory reporting of motor neurone disease (MND) cases will help researchers understand why there are hotspots in NSW, and what causes the disease.

item.title: ISIS-inspired teen pleads guilty to preparing potential terror attack on Sydney Opera House
item.description: The teenage boy told a Sydney court he was considering carrying out a mass terror attack in the CBD after being radicalised on TikTok and other social media platforms.

item.title: How the AI boom is forcing tech prices higher
item.description: The price of phones, laptops and game consoles are rising thanks to a global shortage of their most important part.

item.title: Geelong Cats coach Chris Scott speaks for first time since club's concussion fine
item.description: Geelong coach Chris Scott insists he is unsure if Jake Kolodjashnij will play for the Cats again following the club's concussion saga.

item.title: Lawyer tells court Bogie triple murder survivor could be 'murderer'
item.description: A lawyer tells the jury in the trial of Darryl Valroy Young that the acts his client stands accused of could have been committed by the man the prosecution says is the sole eyewitness.

item.title: Charles Perrottet defends $150k payment made to his wife for 'flexible' work for lobbyist, ICAC hears
item.description: Charles Perrottet was asked by the NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption whether he agreed $150,000 paid to his wife Anita was a significant figure for work done on a "flexible level".

item.title: Energy regulator rejects Transgrid's billion-dollar bailout bid
item.description: Australia's biggest transmission company's bid to pass a billion-dollar bill on to consumers for a bungled high-voltage power line has been slapped down by the regulator.

item.title: Live: Hadley tells court Jones complainant 'broke down' discussing allegations
item.description: Hadley has been called to give evidence in relation to allegations that Mr Jones kissed and touched a young colleague in 2008, without the man's consent.

item.title: Perth GP receives bravery commendation for disarming axe-wielding attacker
item.description: Fergus McCabe has been commended for bravery after he ran to the aid of his colleague, GP Anna Chaney, after a stalker entered her consulting room and wounded her in stomach, grabbing the axe and restraining the offender until police arrived.

item.title: Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery facing job cuts, but minister unclear on number
item.description: Tasmania's cultural institutions are set to face another blow as the Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery looks to reduce its workforce by 30 per cent, figures refuted by the state government.

item.title: Coroner recommends Albury Hospital fix cross-border communication after Kate Manley's death
item.description: A coroner is recommending a hospital improve its cross-border medical records following an inquest into the death of a 46-year-old patient who waited five hours for transfer.

item.title: Detectives arrested a 38-year-old man in Preston on Tuesday morning as part of an investigation into secret commissions.

item.title: Victoria Police charge man over alleged $424,000 in fraud as part of secret commission investigation
item.description: Two men have been arrested by Victoria Police's anti-corruption taskforce, with allegations one of the men was responsible for more than $424,000 in fraud.

item.title: Man charged after investigation into alleged assault of two-month old baby
item.description: Police charge a man with serious child harm offences following a more than year-long investigation into the alleged assault of a two-month-old baby.

item.title: Fremantle coach Justin Longmuir wants Dockers to stay in the moment ahead of Hawthorn AFL finals clash
item.description: Fremantle is just three wins from the club's first-ever AFL premiership, but coach Justin Longmuir dismisses suggestions he will be using that as motivation heading into the finals.

item.title: Will Marnus Labuschagne's recent fortunes see him out of the Test side?
item.description: After spending years as one of the luckiest Test cricketers in the game, Marnus Labuschagne's fortunes appear to be turning and, unfortunately for him, so has his form.

item.title: Cost of building a home rise by almost 30 per cent in five years, Insurance Council of Australia finds
item.description: According to a report released by the Insurance Council of Australia, the cost to build a home in Australia has risen almost 30 per cent in five years.
